mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stop falling and begin rising from their current depressed levels, weekday foot traffic should recover and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if commuting remains weak despite a clear rebound in both series.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase for at least two consecutive weekly observations.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in TRANSIT below zero signals weakening shared mobility and lower incidental shopping trips, which should push RETAIL_REC down within one week. The signal fails if retail remains flat after transit turns negative.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below 0 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days after TRANSIT crosses below 0 and stays negative.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES remain below baseline, people substitute home-centered routines for discretionary outings, reducing retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks. The hypothesis fails if retail rises despite the home-work split persisting.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays above its recent 4-week mean over the next 14 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline and WORKPLACES remains below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS use relative to the recent baseline captures outdoor leisure substitution, and that substitution should pull some discretionary spending away from indoor retail over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if park visits rise but retail activity also rises.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days even though PARKS remains above its last-4-week average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC from their current levels indicates broader discretionary caution; if grocery trips weaken, routine stop-and-shop behavior also weakens and retail-recreation mobility falls over the next two weeks. The claim fails when grocery trips rebound without retail improving.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls more than 3 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decrease within 14 days after a weekly drop in GROCERY_PHARM of more than 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains below baseline for another month, wage-linked daytime spending and lunch-time shopping stay weak, keeping RETAIL_REC lower than in the prior four weeks. The mechanism fails if retail rises while workplace mobility stays depressed.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the last 28 days even though WORKPLACES stays below 0 throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT recovers while RESIDENTIAL eases back toward baseline, it indicates fewer stay-at-home constraints and easier access to shopping corridors, which should raise RETAIL_REC within four weeks. The signal fails if transit improves but residential remains elevated and retail does not respond.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above 0 percent change after being negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days after TRANSIT turns positive and RESIDENTIAL moves back toward baseline.

mechanism_narrative: During a steady cooling or monsoon-disruption regime, persistent weakness in PARKS and TRANSIT points to fewer leisure and shopping trips overall, which should drag RETAIL_REC down over the next one to two weeks. The hypothesis fails if retail rebounds while both mobility series remain weak.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 to 14 days while PARKS and TRANSIT both remain below their recent 4-week means.
